_meta.description: Quest dialogue for MQ-19: The Beacon Summit. Year 2 Spring — political alliance forging.

lines.speaker: npc_linden
lines.text: Jack — the Thornwall envoy is here. And she's not alone. Representatives from three other Beacon Towns arrived with her.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: Commander Janis Beaumont, representing the Beacon Council. Mayor Linden, thank you for hosting us.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: I won't mince words. We've been watching your settlement with interest — particularly your Combat Mech. The Council believes Coppervale could be a strategic asset against the Iron Marauders.

lines.speaker: npc_linden
lines.text: We're not just an 'asset,' Commander. We're a town. With people.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: Of course. Which is precisely why I'm here in person rather than sending orders by radio. This needs to be a partnership, not a requisition.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: The situation is this: the Iron Marauders have unified under a single commander they call 'The Marshal.' He's been absorbing smaller raider bands for two years.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: Our intelligence suggests he's building a real army. Disciplined. Equipped. With salvaged Pre-War military hardware.

lines.speaker: npc_harrow
lines.text: I've seen their scouts. She's not exaggerating. This isn't raiders anymore — this is a military force.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: The Council proposes a formal defense alliance. Shared intelligence, coordinated patrols, and — most critically — shared technology. Your mech designs in exchange for our supply networks.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: So, Jack — what does Coppervale bring to the table? How should we structure this alliance?

choices.text: Full partnership. We share everything — designs, resources, intelligence. No secrets.
We'll share defensive tech, but our advanced mech designs stay in Coppervale. We built them, we control them.
Before we talk about sharing, I want to know — what happened when the Marauders hit Thornwall? Why didn't you fight back then?

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: That's... more generous than I expected. The Council will be pleased. Full transparency builds real trust.

lines.speaker: npc_harrow
lines.text: Bold move, Jack. I hope it pays off.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: Understandable. But defensive tech alone won't win a war. The Council may be... less enthusiastic with their support.

lines.speaker: npc_linden
lines.text: It's a reasonable starting point, Commander. Trust is earned, not given.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: ...A fair question. When the Marshal's raiders first hit our northern outpost, the Council debated for three days before responding. By then, 40 people were dead.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: That failure is why I'm here. Not to repeat it. The Marshal succeeds because we're fractured. He picks us off one by one while we argue about jurisdiction.

lines.speaker: npc_harrow
lines.text: Good answer. I've seen that tactic before. Unity is the only counter.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: If I may interject. I have been analyzing the Marshal's movement patterns from Captain Harrow's intelligence reports.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: He is not raiding randomly. He is systematically securing Pre-War military installations. Bunkers, armories, communication hubs. He is looking for something specific.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: Your AI can analyze strategic patterns? That's... that changes the equation considerably.

lines.speaker: dejin
lines.text: I was built for it, Commander. Though I confess the context has changed somewhat from my original parameters.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: Then we have an accord. The Beacon Council formally recognizes Coppervale as an allied settlement. I'll be staying on as the Council's liaison.

lines.speaker: npc_linden
lines.text: Welcome to Coppervale, Commander. I think you'll find we're full of surprises.

lines.speaker: npc_janis
lines.text: Please — call me Janis. If we're going to war together, formality seems... counterproductive.

lines.speaker: npc_spark
lines.text: Did she just smile? I think she smiled! This is going to be interesting.
